_doc: Vortex (land 99) schedule for phase 1 = Global at the end of Oct 2014. Windows are in the game's clock (UTC + utc_offset_hours, the PST the client shows as Server Time). weekdays: 0 = Sunday ... 6 = Saturday (empty = every day); hours: [start, end) pairs within the day (empty = all day); cycle_weeks + weeks: an event rotation (weeks start on Monday, numbered from 1970-01-05, so week N means the same calendar week for every entry); dates: [from, to] YYYY-MM-DD for a one-off; missions: only these missions of the dungeons (empty = all of the phase's); key: a dungeon key id (dungeon_keys.json): the dungeon is listed at all times and enterable, with the missions of the key tier used, only while the player's window runs (gimuserver/gme/Keys.hpp, DungeonKeyUse). The server turns the open entries into PermitPlace records (land 99, area, dungeon, missions) with the seconds left and the period text (gimuserver/gme/Vortex.hpp); GET /bfanew/vortex?at=YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM shows what is open. Sources: the Sept/Oct 2014 mission captures of cheahjs/bravefrontier_data (their file names carry the capture time, UTC+8: Phantom Pots on Tuesday PST, Box of Desires Wednesday, the Ruins Thursday, Super Metal Parade on weekends, the Sibyl Sisters two days each from Oct 6 to 12, Deemo Oct 1-6, Miku Oct 9-10, Trial of the Gods and Grand Gaia Chronicles from Oct 17-18, Unholy Tower from Oct 22, XE Prologue Oct 23), the 2014 gamelytic farming guide (Monday karma, Tuesday Faerie Paradise, Wednesday Box of Desires, Thursday Oasis of the Gods, Friday Horde of Relics, weekend Golden Vault), the Europe wiki's daily pages (the 2014 energy costs: Sacred Land of the Souls 13/20/25, not the 2017 Soul Sanctuary) and the Global wiki's event archive (Metal keys Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri and Jewel keys Wednesday, the 1st Anniversary from Oct 29). The Parades are opened by keys like the original (one key an hour; the key table hands a Metal Key out on Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri and a Jewel Key on Wednesday). Guesses: Ruins of Light and Dark on Monday (one capture), and the six-week event rotation (each 2014 event ran about a week; the order is ours).
